Consider the matrices $A$ and $Σ$ shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the matrices $U$ and $V?$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $\Sigma$ shown above. Given that $A=U \Sigma V^T$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$  find the matrices $U$ and $V.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's find the singular value decomposition of $A$ using the usual algorithm.

- **Step 1.** Compute $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -24 \\ -24 & 73\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step 2.** Find the singular values: From the matrix $\Sigma,$ we deduce that $\sigma_1=9$ and $\sigma_2=1.$

- **Step 3.** Find the right singular vectors of $A$ (i.e., the unit eigenvectors of $A^T \! A$):

- For $\lambda_1=\sigma_1^2=81,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-81I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -24 \\ -24 & 73\end{aligned}]-81[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-72 & -24 \\ -24 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A^T \! A - 81I)\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{0}$ gives a unit eigenvector
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14181573/assets/720895b40e49950b03d402a7bae8b57c5ed5ea36ea5d4f185b31ed72c7738941.svg)

- For $\lambda_2=\sigma_2^2=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A-I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -24 \\ -24 & 73\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 & -24 \\ -24 & 72\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A^T \! A - I)\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{0}$ gives a unit eigenvector
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14181573/assets/99d869d73edeb6793fc59d1cac03a32f3ddbe20e150e253123a60ebb15040b5e.svg)

- **Step 4.** Find the left singular vectors of $A$: Since we know the singular values and right singular vectors, we can compute the columns of $U$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\mathbf u_1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{1}}A{v}_{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}\frac{27}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute $\mathbf u_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{2} & =\frac{1}{{\sigma }_{2}}A{v}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we construct the matrices $U$ and $V\mathbin{:}$
